title: fix(runtime,cli): one file-URL filename rule for both hosts — FILE: strips case-insensitively, file://NAME opens NAME on the CLI host
body:
Fixes #23794
Fixes #23796
Clause-②: yes

## What changed

One rule turns a SQLite database URL into a file name, and both hosts call it.

- **Runtime host, #23794's half (commit `9c5853767`).** `sqliteFilenameFromUrl` in `packages/runtime/src/standalone-stack.ts` strips `file:` / `file://` case-insensitively on its `sqlite` path, as `detectDriverFromUrl` classifies (`/^file:/i`) and as its `sqlite-wasm` path already stripped. The function is now exported from `@objectstack/runtime` (one name added to the existing standalone-stack export line in `packages/runtime/src/index.ts`). Nothing else in `standalone-stack.ts` moved: not `detectDriverFromUrl`, not `createStandaloneStack`'s `mkdirSync` arms, not its config schema.
- **CLI host, #23796's half (commits `71b52fdbf`, `48728977b`).** `resolveStorageDefinition`'s `sqlite` and `sqlite-wasm` arms in `packages/cli/src/utils/storage-driver.ts` drop their local copy (a case-sensitive `/^file:/` strip, plus `/^sql:\/\//` on the sqlite arm and `/^wasm-sqlite:\/\//` on the wasm arm) and call one module-private helper, `sqliteFileFor`: `normalizeDatabaseUrl`, then the runtime's `sqliteFilenameFromUrl`. A URL the rule refuses is re-raised as `UnsupportedDriverError` (recognized, `driverType` = the kind) carrying the runtime host's sentence minus its `[StandaloneStack]` tag, the shape the CLI host's retired-engine URL refusal took on main. The class is load-bearing: `serve.ts` re-throws `UnsupportedDriverError` and silently swallows every other construction error, so passing the runtime's plain `Error` through would have booted with no storage at all.
- One changeset, `.changeset/23794-file-url-filename-rule.md`: `@objectstack/runtime` minor (the new export, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`), `@objectstack/cli` patch.

## #23794's open question, measured

The card left this unmeasured: does the CLI host strip the prefix the same way? It does not. At base `3fed1eb00`, `OS_MODE=off OS_DATABASE_URL=FILE:./urd.db os serve --dev` made a `FILE:.` directory on the CLI host as well (listing below). The one shared rule fixes both hosts.

## Disk proof at the public door

Every probe ran in a scratch directory outside any repo tree, with the built CLI (`node packages/cli/bin/run.js`) and `OS_HOME` pointed into that scratch directory. Before = base `3fed1eb00`; after = this branch (CLI closure rebuilt).

| host · input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| runtime host, plain project: `OS_DATABASE_URL=FILE:./urd.db os serve` | directory `FILE:.` holding `urd.db` (700416 bytes) | `./urd.db` (700416 bytes), no `FILE:` entry |
| runtime host, control: `OS_DATABASE_URL=file:./urd.db os serve` | `./urd.db` | (unchanged path) |
| CLI host (`OS_MODE=off`): `OS_DATABASE_URL=file://proc/os23794-probe.db os serve --dev` | `Server is ready`, then `[driver-sqlite-wasm] Writing //proc/os23794-probe.db to disk failed (ENOENT …)` for the main and telemetry files; nothing created under the cwd | `./proc/os23794-probe.db` plus its telemetry sibling under the cwd, no write failures |
| CLI host: `OS_DATABASE_URL=FILE:./urd.db os serve --dev` | directory `FILE:.` holding `urd.db` and `urd.telemetry.db*` | `./urd.db` and `./urd.telemetry.db*`, no `FILE:` entry |
| CLI host: `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite OS_DATABASE_URL=postgres://PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@127.0.0.1:5999/db os serve --dev` | `Server is ready`; directories `postgres:/PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@127.0.0.1:5999/` created, holding `db` and `db.telemetry.db*` | exit 1, `✗ sqlite driver was selected but the URL does not look like a file path (its scheme is "postgres://"). Use file:/path/to/db.sqlite, or set OS_DATABASE_DRIVER explicitly.`; nothing created; `PLACEHOLDER` appears 0 times in the output |

The runtime-host boots stop afterwards on the unrelated production prerequisite `OS_SECRET_KEY`, before and after alike, as the card recorded. The `/proc` aim of the CLI-host probe is kept so nothing could be written under `/`.

## What each host answers, before and after (mechanism assumption 1)

`resolveDriverType` + `resolveStorageDefinition(…, { isDev: true })` for the CLI host and `resolveStandaloneDatabase` for the runtime host, same `OS_DATABASE_URL`. Before = base; after = this branch. `kind (file)`; a refusal shows the thrown class.

| driver · URL | CLI before | CLI after | runtime before | runtime after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| - · `file:./x.db` | sqlite `./x.db` | sqlite `./x.db` | sqlite `./x.db` | sqlite `./x.db` |
| - · `file://x.db` | sqlite `//x.db` | sqlite `x.db` | sqlite `x.db` | sqlite `x.db` |
| - · `file:///abs/x.db` | sqlite `///abs/x.db` | sqlite `/abs/x.db` | sqlite `/abs/x.db` | sqlite `/abs/x.db` |
| - · `FILE:./x.db` | sqlite `FILE:./x.db` | sqlite `./x.db` | sqlite `FILE:./x.db` | sqlite `./x.db` |
| - · `File:///tmp/x.db` | sqlite `File:///tmp/x.db` | sqlite `/tmp/x.db` | Error, scheme `"File://"` | sqlite `/tmp/x.db` |
| - · `sqlite:x.db` | sqlite `x.db` | sqlite `x.db` | sqlite `x.db` | sqlite `x.db` |
| - · `sqlite://x.db` | sqlite `x.db` | sqlite `x.db` | sqlite `x.db` | sqlite `x.db` |
| - · `./x.db` | sqlite `./x.db` | sqlite `./x.db` | sqlite `./x.db` | sqlite `./x.db` |
| - · `x.wasm.db` | sqlite-wasm `x.wasm.db` | sqlite-wasm `x.wasm.db` | sqlite-wasm `x.wasm.db` | sqlite-wasm `x.wasm.db` |
| - · `:memory:` | sqlite `:memory:` | sqlite `:memory:` | sqlite (no file) | sqlite (no file) |
| - · `file://x.wasm.db` | sqlite-wasm `//x.wasm.db` | sqlite-wasm `x.wasm.db` | sqlite-wasm `x.wasm.db` | sqlite-wasm `x.wasm.db` |
| - · `FILE:x.wasm.db` | sqlite-wasm `FILE:x.wasm.db` | sqlite-wasm `x.wasm.db` | sqlite-wasm `x.wasm.db` | sqlite-wasm `x.wasm.db` |
| - · `WASM-SQLITE://w.db` | sqlite-wasm `WASM-SQLITE://w.db` | sqlite-wasm `w.db` | sqlite-wasm `w.db` | sqlite-wasm `w.db` |
| - · `wasm-sqlite://` | sqlite-wasm (empty name) | sqlite-wasm `:memory:` | sqlite-wasm (no file) | sqlite-wasm (no file) |
| sqlite · `postgres://u:p@h/db` | sqlite `postgres://u:p@h/db` | **UnsupportedDriverError**, scheme `"postgres://"` | Error, scheme `"postgres://"` | Error, scheme `"postgres://"` |
| sqlite · `sql://x.db` | sqlite `x.db` | **UnsupportedDriverError**, scheme `"sql://"` | Error, scheme `"sql://"` | Error, scheme `"sql://"` |
| sqlite · `libsql://pin.turso.io` | sqlite `libsql://pin.turso.io` | **UnsupportedDriverError**, scheme `"libsql://"` | Error | Error |
| sqlite · `file:` | sqlite (empty name) | **UnsupportedDriverError**, names no file | Error, names no file | Error, names no file |
| sqlite · empty or blank | sqlite (empty name) | sqlite `:memory:` | unified default file | unified default file |
| sqlite · unset | sqlite `:memory:` | sqlite `:memory:` | unified default file | unified default file |

### Behaviour changes on the CLI host beyond `file://` and `FILE:` (reported, not hidden)

1. **Newly refused, fatally:** an explicit `sqlite` selection over a URL with a `SCHEME://` that is not `file:` (`postgres://`, `libsql://`, `wasm-sqlite://`, any other), and a `file:` / `FILE:` naming no file. The first used to boot "ready" and create directories named after the URL, credentials included (measured above); the second declared an empty file name. Both are what the runtime host already refused for the same input. Remedy in the changeset: point `OS_DATABASE_URL` at a file, or select the driver the URL is for.
2. **The undocumented `sql://` strip is gone.** It was reachable only under an explicit `sqlite` selection (URL inference refuses `sql://` as an unknown scheme). `git grep` over the tree finds no other `sql://` spelling. It is now refused like any other non-file scheme; the changeset says to write `file:`.
3. **An empty or blank URL under an explicit `sqlite` / `sqlite-wasm` selection is read as absent: `:memory:`.** It used to be an empty file name. Blank is absent the way `inferDriverTypeFromUrl` reads it; without this the rule would refuse it with "it names no file after `file:`", a sentence about something the operator never wrote. `wasm-sqlite://` with nothing after it is `:memory:` the same way, by the runtime rule's own empty answer for the WASM kind.

## Public surface (mechanism assumption 2)

- `packages/runtime` has no API-surface snapshot or export ledger: its `package.json` declares `build`, `dev`, `typecheck`, `check:test-typecheck`, `gen:test-typecheck-debt`, `test`, `test:repo`; the `api-surface/` snapshot and `check:exported-any` are `packages/spec`'s. Repo gates reading built output (`check:dts-closure`, `check:published-files`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`, `check:lean-entry-closure`, `check:published-readme-exports`) take no registration for a new named export. `check:exported-any-returns` would flag an `any` return; the export returns `string`.
- Downstream typecheck sweep not needed, with evidence: the delta is one added named export whose name collides with nothing. `git grep` finds no `export * from '@objectstack/runtime'` in this repo or in `../objectui`, so no consumer can meet a star re-export ambiguity, and no other symbol is named `sqliteFilenameFromUrl`. The one consumer that imports it, `@objectstack/cli`, was typechecked against the rebuilt `.d.ts` (below).

## Verification

Local runs are on the head named in each line; CI runs the full farm.

- **Runtime pins** (`packages/runtime`): `resolve-project-database.test.ts` (an `it.each` over `FILE:./x.db`, `File:///tmp/x.db`, `FILE://x.db`, `FILE:./x.wasm.db` and the lower-case / bare-path CONTROL rows, asserting `driver` and `sqliteFile`; a bare `FILE:` refused as plain `Error` with the names-no-file sentence) and `standalone-stack.test.ts` (`createStandaloneStack` from an empty cwd over `FILE:./upper/x.db` declares `./upper/x.db`, equal to the `file:` spelling, and the cwd holds no entry matching `/^file:/i`).
- **CLI pins** (`driver-vocabulary-parity.test.ts`, alias block): `file://x.db`, `file:///var/lib/objectstack/x.db`, `file://x.wasm.db`, `FILE:./x.db`, `File:///var/lib/objectstack/x.db`, `FILE:./x.wasm.db` (plus the lower-case and bare-path controls) open the same file on both hosts, dev and prod; both hosts refuse explicit `sqlite` over a credentialed `postgres://` URL, `file:` and `FILE:`, the CLI's refusal an `UnsupportedDriverError` with `recognized: true`, `driverType: 'sqlite'`, a message equal to the runtime's minus its tag, never the runtime's verbatim, and with no credential; the blank-URL reading on the CLI host.
- **Runs on the final head `48728977b`** (after merging `origin/main` at `1eac7ad75`; every heavy run through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, verdict lines quoted):
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime test` (vitest `local` project): `Test Files 399 passed (399)`, `Tests 5990 passed | 19 skipped (6009)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2 src/utils/driver-vocabulary-parity.test.ts src/utils/storage-driver.test.ts src/commands/database-driver-allowlist.pin.test.ts src/utils/dev-self-heal-host-parity.test.ts`: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 188 passed (188)`, `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The allowlist pin is in the set because it uses `resolveStorageDefinition('sqlite', { databaseUrl: 'libsql://pin.turso.io' })` as an oracle: it now answers through the new typed refusal (`recognized: true`, `driverType: 'sqlite'`) and still derives `sqlite`. The CLI `integration` tier is declared to CI: the diff touches no integration-tier file and no spawn entry.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime typecheck && pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck`: `VERDICT command-exit 0`; both `check:test-typecheck: OK` with their debt ledgers held.
  - `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` over the six changed `.ts` files: exit 0, no output. The repo-wide lint run is the PR's `Lint & Repo Gates` check-run.
  - Derived gate families: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (65 commands), each run once with its exit code captured before any pipe: 65 of 65 `exit 0`. Reconciled with `--ran`: `65 derived, 65 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN` (`a DERIVED zero — all 65 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3`). Also `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` (spec moved on `main`'s side of the merge): exit 0, `All 14 generated artifacts are up to date`.
- **Ablations** (run on `71b52fdbf`, before the merge and the tag-strip follow-up, neither of which touches the mutated lines), each through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (anchor hit 1 time, blob changed, restored to the `HEAD` blob with `git diff HEAD` empty). Both subjects are reached through relative source imports (the runtime pins import `./standalone-stack.js`, the parity file imports `./storage-driver.js`), so neither needed a `dist/` rebuild.
  - Runtime: `/^file:(\/\/)?/i` back to `/^file:(\/\/)?/` on the `sqlite` path: `Tests 5 failed | 63 passed (68)`. Red: the `FILE:./x.db`, `File:///tmp/x.db`, `FILE://x.db` rows, the bare-`FILE:` refusal, and the `createStandaloneStack` case (`expected 'FILE:./upper/x.db' to be './upper/x.db'`). The lower-case and bare-path CONTROL rows stayed green.
  - CLI: `return sqliteFilenameFromUrl(url, kind);` replaced by the old local strip `return url.replace(/^file:/, '');`: `Tests 9 failed | 90 passed (99)` in the parity file. Red: the six `file://` / upper-case rows and the three refusal rows. The `sqlite:` / `sqlite://` rows, the lower-case and bare-path controls and the blank-URL case stayed green.
- **Reverse verification of the cross-package type** (on `71b52fdbf`): with the CLI call changed to `sqliteFilenameFromUrl(url, 'postgres')`, `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/cli` failed with `error TS2345: Argument of type '"postgres"' is not assignable to parameter of type '"sqlite" | "sqlite-wasm"'`, so the CLI read the rebuilt runtime `.d.ts`; restored and re-checked as above.

## Acceptance notes

- **Out of scope, measured at the public door, for the seat to file:** the rule's `sqlite-wasm` kind refuses nothing. On the runtime host, `OS_DATABASE_DRIVER=sqlite-wasm OS_DATABASE_URL=postgres://PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@127.0.0.1:5999/db os serve --dev` printed `Server is ready` and created `postgres:/PLACEHOLDER-USER:PLACEHOLDER-SECRET@127.0.0.1:5999/db` under the cwd: credentials in a directory name, against the module header's rule that a URL is never treated as a file path to make bogus directories. The CLI host's wasm arm gave the same file name before this PR and gives it now by the same rule (table rows `sqlite-wasm · libsql://…`). Not fixed here: the refusal for the WASM kind is its own wording and behaviour decision, and this card's surface is the `file:` strip.
- The two hosts still differ on an **absent** URL under an explicit `sqlite` selection: the CLI host's legacy path opens `:memory:`, the runtime host its unified default file. That difference predates this PR (rows "unset" and "empty or blank" above) and is not judged here.
- `#23796` recorded a `[driver-sqlite-wasm]` prefix on write-failure lines while the banner read `SqlDriver(better-sqlite3)`; the base-tree probe here showed the same pairing. Not investigated.
- `origin/main` moved to `a31ff2eb5` after the merge, by two commits that touch neither changed file nor `storage-driver.ts`'s neighbours (scaffold `create` / `init` and translations); not merged, the merge queue rebuilds on the current `main`.

Overlap, in non-closing sentences: #23765 (`detectDriverFromUrl`, another dev's) is untouched here, as are its parity rows. #23737's `mkdirSync` arms in `createStandaloneStack` are untouched. #23792's memory-URL refusal landed on main as PR #23840 before this PR opened; `origin/main` was merged at `1eac7ad75` and both sides kept. #23633's `sqlite://` alias fix is the twin this completes for `file://`.
